propositions: Patch-set upload events are delivered at-most-once by Gerrit webhooks and permanently dropped when the reconciler cursor advances past them without voting, causing changes to stall indefinitely until a manual recheck-review or rebase re-triggers an event.

The reconciler's cursor is an unconditional low-water mark advancing to the newest event in every pass, regardless of whether candidates in that window were voted or abandoned with retryable errors, making them unreachable in future passes.

A change with a retryable failure (timeout, deferred, error) is not re-driven on the next reconciler pass because the cursor has already advanced past its event time, violating the contract that the reconciler re-drives abandoned candidates.

The /health endpoint and reconcile_done output do not expose queue depth, held-back candidates, or which changes are dropped, making the three states (queued, running, never-queued) indistinguishable to operators.

The test suite's fake events-log does not honor the since parameter, so the cursor-advancement defect is never exercised and passes with a false green despite the production code unconditionally advancing to newest.
